notes: Five competitiveness improvements in one release, all gated offline. Search: a cross-session FTS5 recall surface (BM25 plus a 14-day recency half-life) over transcripts and memory slots, wired into the session search and a read-only console block; a forgotten source can never be a hit, an unreadable suppression ledger fails closed with zero hits, and a damaged index rebuilds without resurrecting anything. Steering: follow-up instructions can now be queued while a long turn is running and merge into it at the next iteration instead of waiting for the turn to end; the queue is bounded, survives a crash without losing or duplicating a message, and is checked against suppression both when it is accepted and again when it merges. Memory timeline: learn and restore now leave a bounded, hash-only revision journal (never the body text), surfaced as a per-entry history in the memory view, so an owner can see that an entry changed without the journal becoming a second place where suppressed text could leak. Performance: the body layer is cached read-only and warmed in the background (first-answer body build 21.6ms to 9.4ms, zero file opens on the warm path), chat history is paged in bounded 64KB reverse chunks (transcript read 3.6ms to 0.09ms, response payload 71.9KB to 14.4KB) with an older-messages button and skeletons, and session append was measured at one byte read per write and left alone. Interface: an amber banner keeps the current write target visible, Ctrl/Cmd+K opens a command palette with a real focus trap, consecutive tool calls collapse into one compact line with reasoning folded to a single quiet line, and the mobile bottom sheet gains a spring close. Counts: 3184 core, 631 console smoke, 1980 locale keys, 57 modules, ~35.7k lines.
